label: thm:BC_DMC
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:BC_DMC}
The commitment capacity of a non-redundant DMC $\mathcal{V}$ is the maximal equivocation of the channel over all input distributions:
\[
C_{\text{BC}}(\mathcal{V})=\max_{p_X} H(X|Y),
\]
where $H(X|Y)$ denotes the conditional entropy, the average uncertainty about the transmitted input given the output.
head: environment
name: Commitment capacity for DMCs

label: thm:RID
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:RID}
For any memoryless point-to-point channel $\mathcal{W}$, the identification capacity defined in the exponential scale equals the Shannon transmission capacity defined in the linear scale:
\[
\ddot C_\text{ID}(\mathcal{W})=\max_{p_X}I(X;Y)=C_\text{T}(\mathcal{W}),
\]
where $I(X;Y)$ denotes the mutual information between the channel's input and output.
head: environment
name: Randomised identification capacity

label: thm:DI_DMC
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:DI_DMC}
Given an injective (a.k.a.~reduced) DMC $\mathcal{V}'$ the DI capacity defined in the linear scale is 
\[
C_\text{DI}(\mathcal{V}')=\max_{p_X}H(X)=\log[\#_\text{row}(\mathcal{V}')]
\]
where $H(X)$ is the usual Shannon entropy of the input maximised over all input probability distributions, which is equal to the number of distinct rows of the reduced channel, denoted by $\#_\text{row}(\mathcal{V}')$.
head: environment
name: DI capacity for DMCs

label: thm:DI_continuous
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:DI_continuous}
Let $\mathcal{W}$ be a channel with continuous input alphabet $\mathcal{X}$ and discrete output $\mathcal{Y}$, and let $\widetilde \mathcal{X}=\mathcal{W}(\mathcal{X})$ denote the input image. Then the DI capacity in the linearithmic scale satisfies
\[
\frac{1}{4}d_M\left(\sqrt{\widetilde\mathcal{X}}\right)\leq \dot C_\text{DI}(\mathcal{W})\leq\frac{1}{2}d_M\left(\sqrt{\widetilde \mathcal{X}}\right),
\]
where $d_M$ denotes the (lower) Minkowski dimension. For some channels with $d_M=1$ such as the Bernoulli or the Poisson channels, and some channels with continuous input \emph{and} output, such as the Gaussian channel, the capacity is exactly characterised by
\(
\dot C_\text{DI}(\mathcal{W})=\frac{1}{2}.
\)
head: environment
name: DI capacity for continuous channels

label: def:DI_code
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def:DI_code}
An $(n,N,\lambda_1,\lambda_2)$ code for DI over $n$ uses of a noisy channel $\mathcal{W}:\mathcal{X}\to\mathcal{Y}$ is a family $\{(u_i,D_i):i\in[N]\}$ of code words $u_i\in\mathcal{X}^n$ and associated decoding regions $D_i\subset\mathcal{Y}^n$ satisfying, for all $i\neq j\in [N]$,
\[
\mathcal{W}^n(D_i|u_i)\geq1-\lambda_1, \quad \mathcal{W}^n(D_j|u_i)\leq\lambda_2.
\]
Here $\lambda_1$ denotes the maximum probability of missed identification (the receiver tests the word sent but gets a negative outcome on the identification test), and $\lambda_2$ bounds the probability of wrong identification (the words sent and tested are different, but the outcome of the identification test is positive). These $\lambda_1$ and $\lambda_2$ vanish as $n\to\infty$ in reliable DI codes.
head: environment

label: prop:small_projection
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:small_projection}
    Let $\vec{u}\in\mathbb{R}^n$ be a vector in a high dimensional space and $\vec{Z}=(Z_1,\dots,Z_n)$ a random noise vector where $Z_1,\dots,Z_n\sim\mathcal{N}(0,1)$ are i.i.d. standard normal random variables. The projection of the noise vector onto  $\vec{u}$ satisfies:
    \[
    \Pr\left\{\|\Pi_{\vec{u}}\vec{Z}\|_2\geq x\right\}=2\Phi(-x)\leq\sqrt{\frac{2}{\pi}}\frac{1}{x}e^{-x^2/2}.
    \]

label: lemma:LHL
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lemma:LHL}
Let $P_{HB}$ be an arbitrary joint distribution over $\mathcal{H}\times\mathcal{B}$, denote by $F$ a uniformly random element of a $2$-universal family of hash functions $\mathcal{F}\subseteq\{f:\mathcal{H}\rightarrow\{0,1\}^r\}$, and let $U_r$ be uniformly distributed over $\{0,1\}^r$ and independent of $(F,B)$.
Then,
\[
\left\|P_{F(H),F,B}-P_{U_r}P_{F,B}\right\|_{\text{TV}} \leq \frac{1}{2}2^{-\frac{1}{2}\left(H_{\min}(H|B)-r\right)}.
\]

name: Leftover Hash Lemma

title: Remark
body_md: We assume that the participants are \emph{rational}, in the sense that they are interested in completing the commitment task according to its objective. Thus, a participant may deviate from the prescribed protocol whenever doing so may improve their outcome, but not merely to prevent the task from being completed. Without this assumption, commitment cannot be meaningfully guaranteed, since the sender could always provide a wrong opening such that the receiver always discards the commitment, and the receiver could always declare that the commitment has not been accepted in spite of the verification test, trivially defeating the task by refusing to complete it.

label: thm:privacy_ampl_continuous
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:privacy_ampl_continuous}
Given an AWGN channel $\mathcal{G}$ with transmission capacity $C_\text{T}(\mathcal{G})$ and the commitment construction above, we have, for any $\delta>0$ and large enough $n$,
\[
H_{\min}(W^k|Y^n)\geq 
                                               
k-n\left[C_\text{T}(\mathcal{G})+\delta\right].
\]

name: Privacy amplification with continuous side information

label: thm:concealment
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:concealment}
For any $\delta,\gamma>0$, the proposed commitment protocol is $\epsilon_c$-concealing with
\(
\epsilon_c=2^{-\frac12\gamma n\log n}
\)
as long as
\[\hspace{40pt}\dot R_\text{BC}(n)\leq \dot R_\text{DI}(n)-\gamma -\frac{C_T(\mathcal{G})+\delta}{\log n}.\hspace{40pt}\qed\]

label: thm:HBC
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:HBC}
From any reliable $(n,N,\lambda_1,\lambda_2)$-DI code for $\mathcal{G}$ one can construct an $(n,M,\epsilon_c,\epsilon_b,\epsilon_s)$-BC code with 
\[
\epsilon_c=2^{-\frac12 \gamma n \log n},\quad\epsilon_b=\lambda_2,\quad\text{and}\quad\epsilon_s=\lambda_1.
\]
Furthermore, if $\log N$ scales linearithmically, And $\dot R_{\text{DI}}>0$ is an achievable DI rate, then $\dot R_{\text{BC}}=\dot R_{\text{DI}}$ is an achievable commitment rate.
